name: NFCI tightening regime-gate de-risks SPY (loosen re-arm, tighten cross-up exit)
rationale: Thesis: the Chicago Fed NFCI fuses 100+ money/bond/equity/credit/leverage indicators into one weekly PIT composite; a TRANSITION from loose to tight (NFCI crossing up through a fitted threshold) precedes rising risk premia and declining asset values, and embeds leverage + shadow-banking stress that credit_spread alone misses. We hold LONG SPY while financial conditions are loose/re-loosening (NFCI crosses DOWN below a fitted loosen threshold, with VIX not already spiked so we arm BEFORE the vol event) and de-risk to cash on the tightening cross_up — a slow, low-turnover regime gate that desks treat as 'context' not a trigger. The edge is the regime CHANGE, not the drifting level. Disconfirmer 1: ablate nfci vs credit_spread driving the same arm/de-risk — if credit_spread reproduces the result, NFCI adds nothing beyond its credit component (keep the simpler feature). Disconfirmer 2: a raw NFCI LEVEL lt/gt threshold should NOT work; if it does the signal is a drifting-composite artifact (hence we use cross_down/cross_up only). Disconfirmer 3: must beat buy-and-hold SPY net of fees and not merely be 'flat during high-vol months' — controlled by checking a vix_level-only filter does not reproduce it. Disconfirmer 4: PIT integrity uses the ALFRED initial-release vintage (realtime_start), not revised series, so no look-ahead.
catalyst: NFCI crosses down through its fitted loosen threshold (tight-to-loose regime flip) while VIX is calm — arm LONG; exit on the loose-to-tight cross_up.
